items.title: Fatigue‐Resistant Mechanically Interlocked Co‐Crosslinked Polyimide Films for Reliable High‐Temperature Capacitive Energy Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT During long‐term operation, repeated thermal expansion and contraction inevitably generate cyclic thermal stresses that cause dielectric film buckling, cracking, and eventual device failure. As promising candidates for next‐generation dielectric films, polyimides (PIs) are therefore required to combine high energy‐storage performance with mechanical fatigue resistance under coupled thermal, electrical, and mechanical stresses. Here, we report a mechanically interlocked crosslinked topology designed to meet this requirement. A maleimide‐functionalized crown ether monomer (CM) forms mechanically interlocked junctions with PI chains, while co‐crosslinking with a bismaleimide monomer (SiMI) extends these junctions into a three‐dimensional network and creates nanoscale multiphase interfaces through SiMI self‐crosslinking. This topology improves high‐temperature energy‐storage performance and imparts strong mechanical integrity to the PI films, especially resistance to mechanical fatigue. Dielectric‐optimized PI‐CM0.75‐M7.5 achieves a breakdown strength of 600 MV/m at 200°C and maintains η ≥ 90% up to 450 MV/m. Mechanically optimized PI‐CM0.25‐M2.5 shows a Young's modulus of 2.…

items.title: Colorless shape memory polyimide films for flexible optoelectronics
items.abstract: Abstract Transparent polymer substrates for flexible perovskite solar cells and foldable displays must offer high transparency, thermal stability, and active deformability. With the rapid development of intelligent and adaptive flexible electronics, shape memory functionality has emerged as a key requirement for next-generation devices to enable smart behaviors such as self-deployment or morphing. However, although conventional colorless transparent polyimides (CPIs) exhibit outstanding transparency and thermal resistance, they tend to lack shape memory functionality, making it difficult to meet the demands of next-generation intelligent flexible devices such as self-deployable structures. We designed a molecular system using two dianhydrides, one containing a hexafluoroisopropylidene group and one containing ether linkages, and three fluorinated diamines with different rigidities. The hexafluoroisopropylidene and ether units suppress charge-transfer complex formation to enhance optical transparency, while the ether linkages also improve chain flexibility. The varying diamine rigidity enables tuning of thermal properties. Based on this design, colorless shape memory polyimide (co-…

items.title: Unraveling the Impact of Forming Strategies and Sintering Atmospheres on the Tribological Performance of Polyimide
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional design of polymer tribomaterials assumes higher bulk mechanical strength improves wear resistance, but this empirical rule does not always hold due to processing‐induced microstructural heterogeneities, particularly interparticle interfaces governing dry sliding failure. Herein, polyimide samples were prepared by hot compression molding (HCM) and direct forming (DF) in air or nitrogen. Mechanical testing, multicondition tribological evaluation, and atomistic simulations were combined to establish the process–structure–property relationship. Results reveal a pronounced mechanical‐wear paradox, where nitrogen‐sintered DF PI exhibits lower tensile strength than HCM PI, but achieves a lower specific wear rate and reduced maximum frictional interface temperature under identical sliding conditions. Mechanistic analysis shows that the inert nitrogen atmosphere suppresses thermal oxidative degradation and enables robust, ductile interparticle bonding. This interfacial integrity reduces interfacial shear and frictional heat, facilitating a thin, stable protective transfer film on the counterface. In contrast, the fully dense, HCM PI suffers severe adhesive wear driven…

items.title: Laser-Induced Graphene Microarrays for Enhanced Quantitative Precision in Surface-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry
items.abstract: Abstract Laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry offers distinct advantages for biomolecular analysis owing to its high salt tolerance, low sample consumption, and soft ionization capability. However, localized laser−sample interactions are inherently affected by heterogeneous distributions of analytes and materials, leading to substantial variation between measurements. Improving signal precision has therefore long been a central pursuit in mass spectrometric analysis for reliable qualitative and quantitative biomolecular information. Herein, we report a laser-induced graphene (LIG) microarray platform for enhancing analytical precision in surface-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (SALDI-MS). A straightforward thermal confinement strategy enabled high-resolution LIG patterning under CO2 laser irradiation. Using an unmodified commercial laser cutter, monolithic porous LIG domains with feature sizes as small as 60 μm, below the MS laser spot diameter, were directly patterned on polyimide films. The wettability contrast between hydrophilic LIG and hydrophobic polyimide guided analyte accumulation onto SALDI-active LIG spots, which were fully interrogated b…

items.title: Synergistically Enhanced Properties of Polyimide Films via In-Situ Hollow SiO2 Nanospheres
items.abstract: Polyimide (PI) films serving as high-temperature dielectric and structural materials are increasingly required to combine mechanical robustness, thermal stability, and low dielectric properties for advanced electronic packaging. Herein, PI composite films incorporated with 110 nm hollow SiO2 nanospheres were fabricated via in-situ synthesis and subsequent thermal imidization. The optimal comprehensive performance was achieved at a SiO2 filler loading of 10%. Relative to pristine PI, the optimal composite delivered a 33% enhancement in room-temperature tensile strength (reaching 68 MPa), a 28% increase at 200 °C (reaching 64 MPa), and a 64% improvement at 250 °C (reaching 66 MPa). Benefiting from the hollow filler structure, this sample also exhibited enhanced ductility (reflected by a 1.3% rise in elongation at break), the most favorable thermal stability among all specimens, and a 3.5% reduction in relative dielectric constant, collectively achieving the synergistic enhancement of mechanical, thermal, and dielectric properties and rendering the composite a promising candidate for high-temperature electronic insulation applications.

items.title: Janus Ag Nanoskin‐Armored Polyimide Bilayer Separator Enables Efficient Li‐Nucleation Regulation for Dendrite‐Free Lithium Metal Battery
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Uncontrolled lithium (Li) dendrite growth has been regarded as the most critical obstacle for the widespread adoption of Li metal batteries (LMBs), stemming from the preferential nucleation of Li ions (Li + ) at low‐energy‐barrier sites that trigger heterogeneous deposition. Therefore, it is pivotal yet significantly challenging to effectively control Li nucleation and deposition in LMBs. Here, we engineer a Janus Ag nanoskin‐armored polyimide (Ag@PI/PI) bilayer separator by in situ growth Ag nanoparticles on the surface of PI nanofiber and integrating a high‐strength PI nanofiber membrane as the dorsal substrate. Specifically, the Ag nanoskin acts as a three‐dimensional lithiophilic host to seize Li and induce sequential Li nucleation, thereby preventing Li dendrite formation. As a result, the Ag@PI/PI‐Li||Cu cell exhibits a low overpotential of 31.0 mV, high Coulombic efficiency of 98.9%, and prolonged Sand's time of 26.3 h. Significantly, the Ag@PI/PI separator delivers a high Li + transference number (0.70) and exceptional cycling stability (1600 h) in a Li||Li cell. Moreover, the Ag@PI/PI‐based Li||NCM523 cell achieves a remarkable specific capacity of 108.32 mAh g −…

items.title: A Design Strategy for Next-Generation Low-Dielectric Polyimide Materials: Regulating Aggregated Structures via Flexible Biphenyl Side Chains
items.abstract: Abstract The advancement of 5G and 6G communication technologies has introduced stringent requirements for the dielectric properties of the base materials employed in communication devices. Materials exhibiting a low dielectric constant (Dk) and low dielectric loss (Df) are particularly beneficial for signal transmission, as they reduce signal loss and latency. Modulating the molecular structure represents an effective approach to tailoring the dielectric characteristics of polymers. In this study, to concurrently decrease the Dk and Df values of polyimide (PI), we incorporate side chains comprising flexibly linked biphenyl liquid crystal (LC) units. These side chains increase the interchain spacing, thereby enhancing the free volume and reducing PI density, which contribute to lowering Dk. Concurrently, the flexible biphenyl LC moieties spontaneously organize into ordered stacks, promoting the ordered packing of the main polymer chains and effectively diminishing the Df. A series of PI films were synthesized to investigate the influence of side chains on the dielectric behavior. At a frequency of 17.4 GHz, the BPDA/6MPD film demonstrated a Dk value of 2.73 and a Df value of 0.004…

items.title: Synthesis and properties of low-dielectric hydrophobic polyimides containing alkyl groups and ortho ‑phthalic structures
items.source: Journal of Macromolecular Science Part A
items.abstract: In this study, two novel aromatic diamine monomers (TBA and DTBA) containing methyl, tert‑butyl and ortho-phthalic twisted structures were designed via molecular design. A series of polyimides were subsequently prepared by one‑step high‑temperature solution polycondensation of these diamines with three dianhydride monomers, namely BPDA, BPADA and ODPA, respectively. The synergistic effects of the introduced bulky side groups and twisted non‑coplanar structures on the solubility, thermal properties, mechanical properties, optical transparency, dielectric constant and hydrophobicity of the resulting polyimides were systematically investigated. The results show that all polyimides exhibit amorphous structures and good solubility. Their glass transition temperatures range from 208 to 292 °C, and the thermal decomposition temperatures were above 500 °C, demonstrating excellent thermal stability. Meanwhile, the polyimide films exhibit low dielectric constants (2.77–2.93 at 1 kHz) and good hydrophobicity (water contact angles in the range of 90.7°–99.8°). This study provides an effective molecular design strategy for developing high‑performance polyimides combining low dielectric constan…

items.title: Enhanced mechanical and electrical performance of Ti/Au microelectrode arrays using a pre-cured polyimide substrate
items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents an innovative approach to fabricate flexible neural electrodes with the key characteristics of low impedance and high adhesion. This achievement is realized through a two-step process: first, a thin film metallization process is applied to a partially cured photosensitive polyimide (PSPI) substrate, followed by a full curing process after metal electrode patterning. The proposed method harnesses metal intermixing with the flexible polymer substrate to enhance adhesion. while also utilizing high-temperature curing to rectify lattice defects within the metal-thin film, leading to a notable reduction in impedance. The increase in metal adhesion is empirically confirmed through a scotch tape adhesion test. Furthermore, the effectiveness of impedance reduction is supported by electrochemical characterization, including impedance and phase measurements after complete polymer substrate curing. The impedance of the newly developed flexible neural electrodes is measured at 9.96 kΩ at a frequency of 1 kHz, a marked improvement compared to conventional PSPI-cured electrodes, which exhibit 36.24 kΩ impedance at the same frequency.

Innovative Parasitic Decoupling-Based THz MIMO Antennas for Enhanced Isolation in Advanced 6G Wireless Applications
items.abstract: In this paper, we present a state-of-the-art graphene-based THz Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna, specifically designed for the next generation of 6G wireless communication. The antenna is compact, with overall dimensions of 125×85 µm², and employs polyimide as the substrate material, with a thickness of 4 µm. It operates across a broad frequency spectrum, resonating at 3.98 THz, 5.04 THz, and 6.05 THz, with a substantial bandwidth of 3.44 THz. The design achieves an exceptional peak gain of 13.31 dB and a high efficiency of 96.38%, underscoring its potential for high-performance applications. The antenna's MIMO configuration demonstrates excellent isolation between elements, measured at 35.18 dB, with an Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) as low as 0.00008 and a Diversity Gain (DG) of 9.9996, ensuring robust communication links. This study highlights the antenna's feasibility for THz band applications, positioning it as a strong candidate for integration into future 6G networks.

High-Speed FBG Interrogation for Multi-Point Lithium-Ion Battery Temperature Monitoring Using a REC-DFB Laser Array
items.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries can undergo rapid and spatially nonuniform temperature variations during high-rate operation, requiring multi-point temperature monitoring with high temporal resolution for effective thermal management. This work presents a high-speed fiber Bragg grating (FBG) temperature monitoring system based on a reconstruction-equivalent-chirp distributed feedback (REC-DFB) laser array. The developed 24-channel REC-DFB laser array, integrated with an on-chip optical combiner and semiconductor optical amplifier, achieves a continuous wavelength-sweeping range of approximately 50 nm, with a tuning range of approximately 2.4 nm per channel and channel power equalization. To suppress temperature–strain cross-sensitivity caused by battery deformation, strain-isolated FBG temperature sensors with polyimide packaging are developed, exhibiting sensitivities of 9.7–10.4 pm/°C over 20–80 °C with coefficients of determination (R2) above 0.998. Battery experiments are performed at discharge rates up to 4 C, with simultaneous FBG and thermocouple measurements at the top, middle, and bottom positions. The proposed system achieves an interrogation rate of 5 kHz and shows good agreement…

items.title: Viscosity-regulated sedimentation of gradient CF@Ni/polyimide aerogels for decoupled EMI shielding and microwave absorption
items.abstract: Gradient conductive aerogels are promising for integrated electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding and microwave absorption, yet balancing wave entry, internal attenuation, and shielding effectiveness remains challenging. Herein, monolithic CF@Ni/polyimide aerogels with viscosity-regulated through-thickness filler distributions were fabricated by combining gravity-assisted sedimentation, directional freezing, and thermal imidization. Tuning the solid content of the water-soluble poly (amic acid) salt precursor regulated CF@Ni migration before freezing. Cross-sectional Ni mapping, EDS line scans, and layer-resolved electrical measurements revealed strong filler localization in CPI3, a broadly distributed gradient in CPI5, and a comparatively homogeneous distribution in CPI7. CPI5 achieved the optimal balance between dielectric attenuation and impedance matching, delivering average (SE T ) values of 32.9 and 34.6 dB and power absorption coefficients of 0.82 and 0.97 in the X- and Ku-bands, respectively, together with an (RL min ) of −45.13 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth of 5.55 GHz. items.title: Research on the Patterning Polyimide Layer Based on Laser Ablation Technology
items.abstract: Polyimide (PI) has emerged as a critical material in advanced semiconductor packaging owing to its high temperature stability, low dielectric constant and loss, mechanical flexibility and stress relief, and chemical and moisture resistance. The passivation (PA) layer is usually formed by polyimide-based lithography technology during the whole process of IC packaging, such as bumping packaging, fan-in wafer-level packaging (FIWLP), and fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP). A study on the patterning of a polyimide layer based on laser ablation technology is introduced in this manuscript. A series of samples with the structure of Si substrate/PI layer were prepared, and four different laser ablation conditions were applied to these samples. An inverted trapezoid shape of the opening structure was observed in the PI layer after the effect of laser ablation, which also indicated that the top width was about 6.4 ± 0.6 μm larger than the bottom width according to the measurement data based on scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Research on patterning PI layers based on laser ablation technology could also play an effective role in promoting the popularization of laser ablation technolog…

items.title: A Review of CMOS-Compatible Flexible Biosensors Based on Polymer Electronics for Wearable Healthcare
items.abstract: Flexible wearable biosensors have emerged as a promising technology for continuous, noninvasive health monitoring, driven by the growing demand for personalized healthcare and an aging global population. Polymeric substrates such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyimide (PI), and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) provide lightweight, flexible, and low-cost platforms that conform to the human body, but their practical deployment requires reliable integration with complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) electronics for signal acquisition, processing, and wireless communication. This review summarizes recent advances in CMOS-compatible flexible biosensors, emphasizing polymer-based sensing platforms, circuit-level integration, and system-on-chip (SoC) architectures for wearable healthcare applications. Flexible sensing mechanisms, including electrochemical, capacitive, resistive, and transistor-based devices, are discussed alongside CMOS analog front-end circuits, low-noise amplifiers, analog-to-digital converters, and ultra-low-power signal conditioning techniques. Finally, key challenges in CMOS–flexible sensor integration, including mechanical reliability, biocompatibility,…

items.title: Structurally tunable colorless ionic-type negative-tone photosensitive polyimides with high transparency for i-line photopatterning
items.abstract: With the rapid development of related fields in the semiconductor industry, photosensitive polymers have become an important fundamental material that restricts the manufacturing and quality of integrated circuits and chips. Among various materials, photosensitive polyimides (PSPIs), as a potential alternative to traditional photosensitive materials, have attracted much attention due to their excellent comprehensive performance and the ability to directly serve as a component of micro-nano structures of semiconductor devices. However, traditional polyimide-based photosensitive materials usually exhibit intense yellowing phenomenon due to the formation of charge transfer complexes (CTCs), which adversely affects the sensitivity, resolution and contrast of the photosensitive patterns. With the expanding demand for colorless and highly transparent application fields, how to effectively reduce the CTCs effect while maintaining the photosensitive activity has become an urgent issue to be addressed. items.title: Tailoring the Orientation of Electron‐Delocalized Conjugated Structures in Polyimide Dielectrics for High‐Temperature Capacitive Energy Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric polymers for high‐temperature capacitive energy storage require both high thermal stability and electrical insulation. Although the rigid conjugated structure of polyimide affords a high glass transition temperature, making it a promising candidate, it also introduces compromised electrical insulation through electron delocalization. Here, we propose and demonstrate that regulating the spatial orientation of localized π‐containing/electron‐delocalized conjugated structures in polyimide can effectively break the trade‐off between thermal stability and electrical insulation. The out‐of‐plane orientation of localized conjugated structures reduces the spatial connectivity of short‐range electron‐delocalization sites along the electric‐field direction, thereby suppressing continuous carrier migration. Consequently, under high temperature and elevated electric field, the out‐of‐plane‐oriented semi‐aromatic polyimide exhibits an electrical conductivity reduced by over an order of magnitude compared to its in‐plane‐oriented counterpart. It achieves a high discharge energy density ( U e ) of 7.16 J cm − 3 with a charge–discharge efficiency ( η ) exceeding 90% at 200°C,…

items.title: MPAB-based colorless and transparent copoly(amide imide)s enabled by dianhydride composition control
items.abstract: Colorless and transparent copoly(amide imide) (Co-CPAI) films were synthesized from N, N′-[2,2′-bis(trifluoromethyl)-4,4′-biphenylene]bis(4-aminobenzamide) (MPAB) and two dianhydride systems composed of 4,4′-oxydiphthalic anhydride (ODPA) with either 1,2,3,4-cyclobutane tetracarboxylic dianhydride (CBDA) or 4,4′-(hexafluoroisopropylidene)diphthalic anhydride (6FDA) to investigate the influence of dianhydride composition on the thermomechanical, optical, and solubility properties. Computer simulated three-dimentional structures suggested that CBDA introduces moderate chain bending and a corresponding increase in free volume relative to ODPA, whereas 6FDA produces a much more twisted and expanded chain conformation with the largest free volume. The intermediate composition (MPAB/ODPA/CBDA or 6FDA = 1.0/0.5/0.5) exhibited the highest thermomechanical performance owing to the synergistic effects of copolymerization, which provide an optimal balance among chain rigidity, conformational irregularity, intermolecular interactions, and free volume. The 6FDA-based copolymers generally exhibited higher glass-transition temperatures, thermal decomposition stability, and mechanical properties,…

items.title: Enhanced cryogenic strain sensing of encapsulated distributed optical fiber sensors for Rayleigh-scattering-based measurements
items.abstract: Abstract Distributed optical fiber sensors (DOFSs) have emerged as key tools for safeguarding the stability and safety of cryogenic structures, attributable to their exceptional sensing performance. However, traditional protective layers used for long-term strain monitoring are unable to meet the demands of cryogenic embedment, primarily due to excessive shear force. Once the embedded DOFSs are damaged or fractured, the resulting strain measurements are rendered invalid. This study addresses the issue by exploring an enhanced strain DOFS encapsulated within minuscule capillary tubing, thereby preserving its mechanical properties in an embedded configuration. A theoretical strain transfer model for a multi-layer packaged DOFS was established to elucidate the effects of mechanical parameters and temperature variations on strain transmission, complemented by extensive mechanical experiments conducted at both room and cryogenic temperatures to inform the design of appropriate packaging processes. In addition, strain measurements from encapsulated DOFSs and polyimide-coated DOFSs were compared under nonuniform thermal stress. Furthermore, the long-term monitoring reliability was verifi…

items.title: Tailoring Backbone Rigidity and Cross-Linking of Photosensitive Polyimides for 3D Printing with Ultralow Dielectric Loss at High Frequencies
items.abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing represents a versatile platform for the development of high-frequency communication electronics. However, existing dielectric polymer inks often fail to simultaneously meet the requirements of low dielectric loss, high thermal stability, and high mechanical robustness. In this work, a photosensitive polyimide (PSPI) was synthesized via an acrylate-grafting acyl chlorination route, incorporating trifluoromethyl, bulky fluorene, and asymmetric diphenyl ether moieties. This molecular architecture facilitates the formation of a highly cross-linked network (with a gel content of up to 94%) and enables solvent-free 3D printing while ensuring ultralow dielectric loss and high thermal stability. The cured PSPI ink exhibits a glass transition temperature of 170 °C and a tensile strength of 71.42 MPa. Benefiting from the rigid polymer backbone and optimized crosslinking network, the cured polymer ink achieves a dielectric loss as low as 0.0070 at 20 GHz, outperforming that of state-of-the-art PSPI polymer inks. Furthermore, the successful fabrication of heterogeneous circuit structures via UV-assisted direct ink writing demonstrates the reliability of this sy…

items.title: Numerical investigation of an SNG metamaterial-based multiband THz biosensor for early non-melanoma skin cancer detection
items.abstract: This article presents a high-sensitivity terahertz (THz) metamaterial absorber–based biosensor for the early detection of non-melanoma skin cancer through refractive index sensing. The proposed sensor consists of a pair of concentric gear-shaped resonators (GSRs) fabricated from gold and integrated on a polyimide dielectric substrate, forming a compact unit cell with a periodicity of 75 µm. The designed metasurface exhibits multi-band resonance characteristics, with the highest absorption reaching 99.99 % at a resonance frequency of 1.4485 THz, demonstrating near-perfect absorption behavior. The structure also achieves a high-quality factor (Q-factor) of 1116.8, indicating strong electromagnetic confinement and excellent spectral selectivity. Comprehensive parametric analyses are performed to optimize the geometrical parameters and evaluate the stability of the absorption response under different polarization angles. The sensing performance is investigated by varying the refractive index of the surrounding medium within the biologically relevant range of 1.35–1.39, corresponding to normal and cancerous skin tissues. The proposed biosensor exhibits a clear and consistent resonance…

items.title: TacClip: a clip-on sensor measures dynamic contact forces without covering the fingerpads
items.abstract: TacClip is a minimally encumbering wearable device for recording fingertip deformation caused by contact forces and vibrations. It can be combined with vision- or glove-based hand tracking systems that leave the fingertips uncovered and provides a measure of dynamic contact interactions, while leaving the finger pads exposed so that the user retains natural sensitivity to texture, friction, temperature, and fine surface features. The signal is produced by a Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) embedded on a small plastic clip mounted over the fingernail. Optionally, for use with vision-based tracking, additional FBGs on polyimide strips can complement camera-based pose estimation. In finger pressing tests, TacClip estimates the force magnitude with typical errors below $0.5~\mathrm{N}$ over a $0$--$8~\mathrm{N}$ range. In tests of cloth handling and tape edge finding, we show that it captures the vibrations and dynamic events generated during exploratory sliding. With no electronics, TacClip can also be used submerged in water, while preserving bare finger contact.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT A series of colorless copolyimide (Co‐PI) films was prepared by one‐step polycondensation of a twisted benzimidazole diamine (1‐(4‐amino‐2‐methylphenyl)‐2‐methyl‐1H‐benzo[d]imidazol‐5‐amine) with HPMDA and CBDA at varying molar ratios. The rigid cyclobutane ring of CBDA significantly influenced the thermal property and dimensional stability of the resulting copolymers. All films exhibited excellent thermal stability with 5% weight loss temperatures ( T d5% ) in the range of 464°C–480°C. The glass transition temperature ( T g ) increased from 448°C to 485°C with rising CBDA content due to restricted chain mobility, while the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) decreased markedly, reaching as low as 38 ppm/K. The copolymer with 50 mol% CBDA offered a balanced performance (CTE = 39 ppm/K) while maintaining high optical transparency. items.title: Time dependent exposure effects in thin film semiconductor technology
items.abstract: Photosensitive polymer films are used in semiconductor manufacturing as dielectric and passivation layers. Their chemical, mechanical, and interfacial properties depend not only on the total exposure dose applied, but also on the temporal characteristics of the exposure, which influence the photochemical reaction kinetics and the formation of the polymer network. Industrial exposure tools deliver the same dose with different intensity–time profiles. It remains an open question whether the commonly held assumption of exposure reciprocity applies to chemically complex systems such as high-performance polyimides. This study examines how exposure intensity and time influence the material behavior of a negative-type, photosensitive polyimide thin film. At the same wavelength and nominal dose, high-intensity Stepper exposure is compared with low-intensity Mask Aligner exposure, so that the two differ primarily in their intensity–time profiles. items.title: Flexible IGZO Field‐Effect Transistor Biosensor Platform for Mechanically Stable and Cortisol Detection
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible field‐effect transistor (FET) biosensors based on amorphous oxide semiconductors are promising approaches for wearable biochemical monitoring. However, achieving electrical uniformity, mechanical stability, and receptor‐mediated specificity simultaneously remains challenging. We report a wafer‐scale fabricated indium–gallium–zinc oxide (IGZO) FET platform on a polyimide (PI) substrate for cortisol detection under liquid‐gated operation. Statistical characterization across 50 devices demonstrates consistent transistor performance, with an average transconductance of 0.326 mS and an average subthreshold swing of 130.75 mV dec − 1 . The devices maintain stable electrical performance under bending radii of 15–30 mm and after 100 deformation cycles. The bare IGZO FET exhibits reversible pH response, confirming stable electrostatic coupling at the semiconductor–electrolyte interface. Following covalent immobilization of a cortisol‐specific aptamer, the device exhibits a concentration‐dependent drain current response from 10 fM to 10 µ m at a constant gate bias ( V G = 0.4 V). items.title: A Compact Three‐Layer VO 2 ‐Integrated Reflective THz Metasurface With Switchable Half‐Wave‐Plate and Quarter‐Wave‐Plate Responses
items.abstract: This paper presents a VO 2 ‐integrated reflective switchable polarization conversion metasurface (SPCM) that exploits the insulator‐to‐metal phase transition of vanadium dioxide (VO 2 ) to achieve binary switching between two distinct polarization conversion modes within a single device. The unit cell consists of a square split‐ring resonator (SSRR) incorporating gold and VO 2 on a 50 μm polyimide substrate, backed by a continuous gold ground plane. When VO 2 is in the insulating state, the metasurface operates as a linear‐to‐circular (LTC) converter with ellipticity approaching + 1 and an axial ratio below 2 dB across 600–685 GHz. In the metallic state, the device switches to linear‐to‐linear (LTL) cross‐polarization converter with a polarization conversion ratio (PCR) exceeding 0.8 over the same band. Unlike prior multifunctional designs that rely on auxiliary graphene biasing or photoexcited semiconductors to access both conversion types, the present design maps each VO 2 phase directly and independently to one conversion mode. Angular stability tests show PCR > 0.60 for incidence angles up to 55° in the LTL state and axial ratio < 3 dB for θ i < 30° in the LTC state.

items.title: Hybrid Flexible–Soft Neural Interface as a Practical Solution for Long‐Term Implants
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Implantable neural interfaces face persistent challenges in long‐term functionality due to chronic immune responses, mechanical mismatch with tissue, and material corrosion in vivo. The commonly used flexible materials, such as polyimide and parylene‐C (poly[monochloro‐ p ‐xylylene]), have advantages in low water vapor permeability and high processing resolution, but their GPa‐level modulus and limited stretchability may lead to fibrotic encapsulation and signal loss. In contrast, soft materials, such as silicones and hydrogels, provide tissue‐like compliance and intrinsic stretchability with a kPa–MPa modulus but have poor barrier properties and fabrication precision. Fortunately, by integrating a flexible thin‐film encapsulation with a compliant soft substrate, hybrid flexible–soft neural interfaces provide a promising approach to overcoming the limitations of both material systems. This review first systematically summarizes flexible and soft neural interfaces, respectively, from materials and properties to lifespan. Then, the latest advances are highlighted in hybrid flexible–soft interface performance across different applications, including superior mechanical stabi…

items.title: Nereis Jaw‐Inspired Pretreatment‐Free Direct Metallization on Pristine Polyimide Films for Flexible Electronics
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface metallization of polyimide (PI) films is essential for constructing conductive electrodes and interconnects in flexible electronics, directly determining device integration and reliability. However, the high inertness and low surface energy of PI necessitate complex pretreatment in conventional vacuum deposition, incurring high costs and substrate damage, while wet etching faces environmental burdens and poor compatibility, both failing to meet large‐scale manufacturing demands. Inspired by the stable coordination of histidine in Nereis jaws, a coordination‐directed molecular design strategy is proposed. By introducing nitrogen‐containing heterocyclic units into PI molecular chains, intrinsic metal anchoring sites are constructed, enabling direct film metallization without destructive adhesion‐promoting surface pretreatments. This process integrates with photolithography, printing, and direct writing for cross‐scale controllable metallization, fabricating planar wiring and vertical interconnect access (VIA) structures for 3D high‐density integration. items.title: Strain control of mid-IR spectroscopic nonlinear photocurrents in PtSe$_2$
items.abstract: Semi-metallic noble-metal dichalcogenides are promising materials for infrared optoelectronics, yet the origin and tunability of their nonlinear optical responses remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate in-situ mechanical control of photon-drag photocurrents in polycrystalline PtSe$_2$ thin films grown on flexible polyimide substrates. Using polarization-resolved mid-infrared photocurrent spectroscopy under uniaxial tensile strain, we observe pronounced strain-dependent changes in resistivity, photoconductivity, and helicity-dependent nonlinear photocurrents. The spectral response is consistent with optical excitations across the spin-orbit-coupling-induced (SOC) band gap near the K point. We develop a theoretical framework attributing the photocurrent primarily to photon-drag induced by photon-momentum symmetry breaking. Strain modifies its magnitude and polarization dependence through deformation potentials that tune the SOC-induced band gap. These results establish mechanical strain as a route toward reconfigurable infrared polarization detection.

items.title: Synthesis of soluble polyimide with high char yield for flame retardant poly(vinyl alcohol)
items.abstract: Abstract Polyimides (PIs) have been attracting increased attention due to their unique advantages, such as excellent thermal stability, good mechanical properties and low dielectric constants. However, poor solubility hinders their further application. To solve this problem, a series of PIs with different side units (–CH 3 , –CF 3 and –COOH) were synthesized, and the relationship between molecular structure and solubility was thoroughly investigated. In general, solubility has been significantly improved, and all the polymers could be dissolved in hot m-cresol and N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP). With increasing polarity of side units (–COOH > –CF 3 > –CH 3 ), the solubility of their corresponding polymers (PI-COOH, PI-CF 3 and PI-CH 3 ) improved, and PI-COOH could be dissolved in alkaline aqueous solutions. In addition, PI-COOH films showed an outstanding comprehensive performance with a high tensile strength greater than 100 MPa, a high initial decomposition temperature of 420.3 °C, a low coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of 9.62 ppm °C −1 and a low dielectric constant of less than 3. PI-COOH also possessed a good charring capacity, and a char yield of 40 % was achieved at a high…

items.title: Advanced Dielectric Polymer Development at Kayaku Advanced Materials
items.abstract: High frequency, 5G+ and edge computing opportunities continue to evolve towards wider adoption. Next-generation dielectric polymeric materials remain crucial to enabling future device packaging designs. The challenge lies in creating a material that balances the necessary characteristics to withstand harsh environments and complex designs. Most importantly, the material’s stability is essential to the performance of the packaged device. Future materials must continue to offer low dielectric loss (Df), low dielectric constant (Dk), and low moisture absorption while maintaining strong mechanical and thermal properties to resist the inherent stresses in the final package. High power devices such as MOSFETs and Si-C and Si-N based transistors require performance criteria of further increased thermal stability and higher break-down voltage, simply due to higher operating temperatures and voltages. Additionally, these emerging materials must be competitively priced and/or easy to manufacture to displace current industry players and manage the complexities of assembly. The resin polymer is often the most critical component among these materials. Therefore, it is essential for suppliers t…

items.title: Low concentration NO 2 gas detection with a flexible, highly sensitive and robust sensor
items.abstract: Abstract Amorphous indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) based flexible and robust chemiresistive NO 2 gas sensors prepared on a polyimide substrate are presented in this work. A different target composition of IGZO (In:Ga:Zn ratio of 1:1:5) than the usually reported In:Ga:Zn:1:1:1 composition for gas sensing is explored in the present study. IGZO (115) composition has been reported for transparent thin film devices and circuits previously. In fact, this is the first study to explore this particular composition for the fabrication of flexible gas sensors. The devices are semi-transparent, adding another functionality that can be useful for see-through devices. Therefore, this study can open new paths for transparent, flexible, and fully integrated all IGZO based devices and circuits. The sensor gives an excellent response to sub-ppm exposures of NO 2 gas. A 262% increase in the resistance of the device is observed for 1 ppm NO 2 exposure at 125 °C which is amongst the best responses reported for metal oxide based flexible NO 2 gas sensors. The sensor device shows a highly linear response ( R 2 = 0.9928) to sub-ppm NO 2 concentrations with an experimentally observable limit of detection…

items.title: Inkjet Printed Interconnections on Flexible Substrates
items.abstract: Utilization of inkjet printing as a manufacturing method in electronics has been studied at Tampere University of Technology. In order to successfully utilize inkjet deposited circuit patterns with traditional electronics components, different aspects must be considered. One of the critical issues is the electrical contact between discrete components and inkjet printed conductive traces. In this study, discrete passive components were joined to conductive traces that were inkjet printed with metalloorganic nano silver ink on flexible substrates such as polyimide foil and polyethylene naphthalate (PEN). Discrete passive components were attached using isotropic conductive adhesive. JEDEC 22-A104C Standard temperature cycling tests as well as shear strength tests were carried out on the manufactured samples. There is a need for information on the reliability of inkjet printed interconnections and this is why accelerated reliability testing was selected as the test method. This also gives information on failure mechanisms of printed interconnections, which is very critical in terms of overall reliability. items.title: Stretch-free, shape-induced 3D Island-Bridge Networks for flexible TFTs on Silicon Planar Technology verified through Bending and Scalability to 9x9 Matrix
items.abstract: This study presents a CMOS-compatible, fully integrated three-dimensional island-bridge concept for flexible electronics on silicon planar technology. By embedding metal bridges within trenches in a polyimide-passivated island matrix, the approach localizes mechanical stress to the bridges whereby active components on the islands are protected from mechanical stress, enabling high-performance thin-film transistors (TFTs) on flexible substrates. A concave, arc-shape forming fill in trenches between the islands and backside etching yield freestanding 3D bridges. Numerical simulations to determine the minimum bending radius reveal a characteristic stress distribution in the bridges during bending, with peak stresses at the bridge-island transitions. Variation of trench depth modulates von Mises stress, identifying design parameters for reliability. Experimental validation demonstrates TFT operation under bending, with stable threshold voltage, subthreshold swing, and saturation mobility across a range of bending radii; broader bridges exhibit enhanced mechanical robustness. items.title: Facile synthesis of high-performance colorless polyimide films bearing amide groups with enhanced optical and thermal stability
items.abstract: The rapid development of flexible displays has spurred the rational design and performance optimization of colorless polyimide films (CPI) with superior integrated properties. In this work, a series of amide-bridged CPI films were fabricated via polycondensation of the as-synthesized dianhydrides ( p -DAMDA, m -DAMDA, F-DAMDA) with commercial diamines, including 2,2′-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzidine (TFDB) and trans-1,4-diaminocyclohexane (t-CHDA). The results demonstrated p -DAMDA/TFDB exhibited the most favorable comprehensive performance, featuring a high optical transmittance of 86% at 550 nm, a low CTE value of 8.7 ppm K -1 and a relatively high T g of 334°C. Besides, the effects of meta-substituted structure and aromatic fluorination on the optical and thermal properties of as-prepared CPI films were systematically investigated. The results showed the aromatic fluorination (i.e., hydrogen atoms substituted by fluorine), effectively enhanced the optical performance while retaining excellent dimensional stability. items.title: Zn–bipyridine structure design for constructing a robust transparent polyimide as the substrate for flexible photodetectors
A Hydrogenated Amorphous Silicon Photodiode indirect flexible device for radiation flux measurements at low intensities
items.abstract: The objective of the Photo-HASPIDE experiment is the construction and test of an indirect a-Si:H (Hydrogenated Amorphous Silicon) photo-detector plus scintillator device on a flexible substrate for the detection and measurement of particles fluxes (X-rays, electrons and protons) and for dosimetric measurements. The idea behind this experimental project lies in the utilization of Hydrogenated Amorphous Silicon (a-Si:H) as photodiode material; owing to its notable attributes of radiation hardness, light detection capability and mechanical flexibility. After the implementation of the HASPIDE experiment, which explored direct radiation detection using a-Si:H devices on a polyimide (PI) substrate, we aim to delve into indirect detection by employing these devices in conjunction with flexible and rad-hard scintillators like polysiloxane. The indirect detector design holds promise for improved responsiveness to low radiation fluxes compared to direct detection methods. The indirect a-Si:H detector should be composed of arrays of small (about 5 x 5 mm2) scintillator crystals read by a-Si:H photodiodes.
